summary: V6.25.9 review — character-aware MacroBuilder + React.createPortal z-index fix. Backend 25/25 pytest pass (5/5 new V6.25.9 token grammar + 5 V6.25.8 mod-rank/genesis + 15 V6.25.7/V6.25.6 regression). Frontend live UI smoke via Playwright CONFIRMED end-to-end: login → BESM campaign → QRB Test 3 sheet → Mechanics tab → empty slot → SlotPicker (portaled to <body>) → New macro → MacroBuilder (portaled to <body>, title 'for QRB Test 3'). Chip click-to-insert wires correctly (stat chip → {stat:body}, dice preset auto-joins with '+', operator appends raw). Live preview substitutes to '+4' for body=4. Modal stays fixed and fully visible after scrolling underlying sheet to bottom (bbox 0,0,1920,1080 persists — z-[200] portal cannot be clipped by ancestor stacking context). Close button works. All V6.25.9 P0 acceptance criteria PASS.

action_items: INFO — All V6.25.9 P0 acceptance criteria PASS. No code changes required from main agent for this cycle.

OPTIONAL — The /api/channels/{chid}/messages curl with body='/strike' & character_id=... was NOT exercised directly via curl this round because pytest already covers the same code path 5/5 (test_attr_token_resolves_effective_level, etc.) using the same POST body shape. If E1 wants a literal curl artefact, happy to add one next round — not blocking.

OPTIONAL — For UI automation of {attr:*}/{skill:*}/{def:*} chip groups, consider seeding a long-lived BESM character with at least 1 attribute + skill + defect (the test_v6259 fixture tears its character down after pytest). Non-blocking.
critical_code_review_comments: MacroBuilder.jsx (~494 lines) is well within the 700-line guideline. Clean separation of ChipGroup/TokenChip/CustomDicePicker/NumericInjector subcomponents + pure helpers at bottom — good.

The _expandClientSide() client mirror of backend _expand_macro_tokens is a maintenance hazard — any backend grammar change must be mirrored here or live preview will desync from fire-time. Recommend adding a short comment block at the top of both mirror functions cross-referencing each other + a shared pytest-style contract test that asserts parity (e.g., a /api/macros/preview endpoint the builder could optionally hit). Non-blocking for this cycle.

MacroBuilder.jsx L70: append() auto-inserts '+' only if lastCh is NOT in '+-*/×÷(' — this is correct for the common case but will still produce '+-N' when appending a negative number after '+'. Acceptable because the backend normalizes '+-' → '-' on L492.
MacroBuilder.jsx L108-321 portal + z-[200] is the correct fix; rendering at document.body guarantees escape from any card-mystic stacking context ancestor (the V6.25.7 bug).
QuickRollBar.jsx SlotPicker now also portaled — good; prevents the same bleed-through for the slot picker itself.

Test file test_v6259_macro_grammar.py exercises Create→Fire verification pattern correctly (POST macro, then POST /messages with character_id, then assert slash_meta.macro.formula_expanded substring) — exemplary.

Minor: _effLevel() default is Math.max(1, ...) which floors effective level at 1. This matches BESM 4E rule (effective level cannot go below 1 via limiter/enhancement arithmetic) — correct. Backend should do the same.

success_rate.frontend: 100% — all V6.25.9 testid contract + portal + scroll-hold behaviours confirmed live via Playwright

Gotchas: (1) Login inputs DO have data-testids ('auth-email-input' / 'auth-password-input') and type='email'/'password' — earlier iter58 note about missing type attrs is STALE. (2) /login URL redirects; use /auth?mode=login or click 'Sign In' from landing. (4) The MacroBuilder and SlotPicker both portal to document.body — any test that expects them under the QuickRollBar ancestor DOM subtree will fail; select by data-testid globally instead.
rca of the issue: No bugs found. The V6.25.7 stacking-context clip (MacroBuilder rendered behind next scroll section) was root-caused by the card-mystic ancestor creating a stacking context that clipped the z-index:50 modal. The V6.25.9 fix — React.createPortal(…, document.body) — is the textbook solution and is verified live: the modal renders as a direct child of <body>, covers the full viewport (1920x1080 bbox) at z-[200], and stays visible over ALL underlying content regardless of window scroll position.
